claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal-based HEA nanoparticles is governed by restricting atomic mobility during high-temperature formation.
Immobilizing metal precursors on a high-surface-area support with abundant surface defects forces nearly simultaneous nucleation of all constituent metals.
Nearly simultaneous nucleation suppresses elemental segregation and produces a uniform HEA phase.
The resulting uniform HEA phase is catalytically active.
Metal precursors can be uniformly deposited from a well-mixed solution onto activated carbon or oxide supports with tailored defects and surface chemistries.
Depositing metal salts under ambient conditions and rapidly heating them under a reducing atmosphere enhances precursor-support interactions.
A brief high-temperature pulse in a reducing environment initiates nearly simultaneous reduction and nucleation of the different precursors.
Strong interactions between metal atoms or precursors and support defects immobilize the metal species.
Support defects act as physical barriers to long-range metal diffusion during the thermal pulse.
Defect anchoring drastically limits atomic mobility during rapid thermal processing.
Enforced localization minimizes the time available for phase separation and elemental segregation.
Compared with a support lacking tailored defects, the enhanced support will yield nanoparticles with a more homogeneous elemental distribution.
Compared with a support lacking tailored defects, the enhanced support will yield more controlled nanoparticle morphology.
Compared with a support lacking tailored defects, the enhanced support will yield higher surface-atom exposure.
A support with suboptimal defect density permits greater atomic mobility and consequently produces phase separation.
A support with suboptimal defect density produces irregular nanoparticle morphology and lower accessible catalytic surface area.
The proposed mechanism applies to metal precursors deposited on engineered high-surface-area supports.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to unsupported or colloidal systems governed by molecular complexation and different diffusion constraints.
